name: Lipomatous hypertrophy of the atrial septum
aliases: lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum

clinicalPearls: A benign, non-encapsulated deposition of mature and brown fat within the interatrial septum, distinct from a true encapsulated lipoma
Characteristically produces a dumbbell or bilobed thickening that spares the fossa ovalis, giving a waisted appearance
Commoner with increasing age and obesity and usually discovered incidentally on echocardiography or cross-sectional imaging
Most cases are asymptomatic, but very bulky deposits can encroach on the atrium or the region of the sinus node and provoke atrial arrhythmias
The brown-fat component is metabolically active and can be FDG-avid on positron emission tomography, a benign appearance that must not be misread as tumour
Cardiac MRI and CT confirm the fatty nature and the typical fossa-sparing shape, distinguishing it from a mass or thrombus
No treatment is needed for asymptomatic disease; intervention is reserved for the rare case causing significant obstruction or refractory arrhythmia
reference.pathophysiology: Lipomatous hypertrophy of the atrial septum is an overgrowth of adipose tissue, including metabolically active brown fat, within the interatrial septum. Because the fossa ovalis contains little fat, it is characteristically spared, so the deposit expands the muscular septum above and below it to create the classic dumbbell shape. The tissue is hyperplastic rather than neoplastic, which explains its benign course, but the brown-fat element takes up glucose and can appear avid on FDG imaging, mimicking malignancy. Extensive deposits may bulge into the right atrium, interfere with the adjacent conduction tissue, and predispose to supraventricular arrhythmias.
additionalDifferentials: Atrial myxoma or other cardiac tumour
Metastatic deposit to the atrial septum
Amyloid or other infiltrative septal thickening
additionalInvestigations: Transthoracic echocardiography showing echobright septal thickening that spares the fossa ovalis
Transoesophageal echocardiography for clearer characterisation of the septal mass
Cardiac MRI with fat-suppression sequences to confirm the adipose nature
Cardiac CT demonstrating fat density and the typical dumbbell morphology
Recognition of benign FDG uptake on positron emission tomography to avoid misdiagnosis as tumour
redFlags: Very bulky deposits causing right atrial inflow obstruction or superior vena cava compromise
Refractory atrial arrhythmias attributable to the septal infiltration
Imaging features atypical for fat that raise concern for a true neoplasm
Rapid growth prompting reassessment of the benign diagnosis
reference.prognosis: The condition is benign and generally carries an excellent prognosis, with most patients remaining asymptomatic and requiring only reassurance and recognition of its characteristic imaging appearance.
pitfalls: Misinterpreting benign FDG avidity as malignancy and pursuing unnecessary biopsy or surgery
Confusing the deposit with an atrial tumour or thrombus
Failing to note the characteristic sparing of the fossa ovalis that confirms the diagnosis
Attributing unrelated symptoms to an incidental, asymptomatic septal deposit
references: Braunwald's Heart Disease: A Textbook of Cardiovascular Medicine
Cardiovascular imaging references on cardiac masses
management: Reassurance with no active treatment for the typical asymptomatic incidental finding
Confirm the benign fatty nature with cardiac MRI using fat-suppression sequences or cardiac CT to exclude a true tumour or thrombus
Recognise benign FDG-avid brown fat on positron emission tomography to avoid misdiagnosis as malignancy and unnecessary biopsy or intervention
Treat supraventricular and atrial arrhythmias, when bulky deposits provoke them, with standard rate or rhythm control and antiarrhythmic therapy
Reserve surgical resection for the rare cases causing significant right atrial obstruction or refractory arrhythmia
Provide periodic imaging follow-up for very bulky deposits that encroach on the atrium or the region of the sinus node
